reason: Tella's Cut panel exposes Remove buffers and Find mistakes that the published CLI didn't cover. Live smoke tests against api.tella.com on 2026-05-16 confirmed both POST shapes return 404 — the public OpenAPI has no equivalent. The web UI calls unofficial hosts: www.tella.tv (`/api/stories/{vid}/scenes/{cl}/silences?mode=...` + apply PATCH) for buffer trimming and prod-stream.tella.tv (`/ai-mistakes/analyze-scene` SSE) for mistake detection. Both unofficial hosts reject the public-API Bearer token with 401 `not_authenticated` and require a session cookie issued to a logged-in browser. This patch composes the documented public endpoints (GET /silences + POST /cut) for Remove buffers / Trim edges, and uses a mixed-auth path for Find mistakes (cookie-auth analyze + Bearer-auth public /cut apply) behind a hard `--unofficial` gate. Side-fix: extractSilenceRanges previously only handled `{start,end}`/`{startMs,endMs}` shapes, missing today's `{startTimeMs,durationMs}` response — that's why `--trim-silences-gt N` had been silently planning zero cuts on the live API. The parser now handles both shapes and the planned cut args now use the spec-correct `{fromMs,toMs}`.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test all clean (24 unit tests across the cli package). Skill verifier: ✓ All checks passed. Live smoke against the test workspace: `videos clips remove-buffers <vid> <cl> --dry-run --min-ms 500` planned 42 cuts from 105 silences; `videos clips trim-edges <vid> <cl> --dry-run` planned head/tail correctly; `videos clips find-mistakes <vid> <cl> --unofficial --detect-only` confirms the unofficial AI service returns detected mistakes when a fresh session cookie is set. Reset via PATCH /clips/{clipId} {cuts:[]} after each mutating run.

reason: A failed write may have committed remotely before the client observed the failure, so replaying a POST/PATCH after a 5xx or dropped connection can create duplicates or start paid work more than once. Authentication rejection and rate limiting are distinct recovery paths and keep their retry budget.
validated_outcome: Ambiguous-failure branches are guarded without disabling the shared retry budget. Ported from mvanhorn/printing-press-library#1978.

reason: Go 1.26.4 carries fixes for reachable standard-library vulnerabilities reported against earlier 1.26 toolchains; the catalog-wide docs floor must match each module go directive.
validated_outcome: Bulk verification confirmed all direct published CLI go.mod files declare go 1.26.4 or newer after the sweep.

reason: Go 1.26.5 carries the standard-library fix for GO-2026-5856; the catalog-wide docs floor must match each module go directive so users do not build published CLIs with a vulnerable Go toolchain.
validated_outcome: Bulk verification confirmed all direct published CLI go.mod files declare go 1.26.5 or newer after the sweep.

reason: The generated gate `flags.asJSON || !isTerminal()` short-circuited explicit format flags when stdout was piped (the agent / shell case). printOutputWithFlags also fed CSV/plain renderers an envelope-shaped JSON instead of a flat array. --quiet was silent despite docs saying 'one value per line'. --plain had no renderer at all.
validated_outcome: videos list --csv --select id,name | head -3 emits CSV header + 2 rows; videos list --quiet --select id emits one ID per line; videos list --plain --select id,views emits tab-separated rows; videos/playlists/clips get --select id,name returns the populated {id,name} object.

reason: The OpenAPI parser (parser.go:4295) only walks top-level response properties when scanning for next_cursor / has_more. Tella's REST envelope nests them under {pagination:{...}}, so Pagination.NextCursorPath and HasMoreField were emitted as empty strings and the --all loop exited after page 1.
validated_outcome: videos list --all returns all 232 videos across 16 cursor-followed pages (was 15).

reason: Tella's public API evolves faster than this CLI's archived spec: timeline/transcript reads, official silence modes, transcript corrections, audio overrides, Studio Voice (the API's studioSound field), and additive resource batches are now supported, while Find Mistakes and whole-clip mute are still not public. Compound cuts must be batched against one playback timeline. Because no conditional cut update exists, failures must report recovery state instead of restoring automatically; snapshots must retain both pre-clean and last-known post-clean cuts so explicit undo refuses after divergence and requires an exclusive-editing confirmation. apply_video_edits must never be treated as a cut API.
validated_outcome: Go 1.26.6 test, vet, build, and govulncheck pass; verify-skill passes; HTTP fixtures cover official payloads, multiple clips, existing cuts, dry-run, apply, explicit restore, partial failure, indeterminate responses, advisory divergence checks, and required exclusive-editing confirmation. Credential-dependent live Tella mutation checks remain explicitly unverified.

reason: The live Tella OpenAPI gained POST /v1/sources, POST /v1/videos/{id}/clips, POST /v1/videos/{id}/clips/{clipId}/cut-by-transcript, and a multi-range body for POST /cut after the original print. These endpoints are the public API path for full editor coverage: uploading source assets, adding clips/B-roll sources, cutting by multiple time ranges, and cutting by transcript word indices. The novel workflow layer composes these primitives into insert-file, add-broll, silence-map, cut-words, replace-word-ranges, storyboard/apply-storyboard, format, audit, and playlist edit-pass so agents can operate the editor at video or playlist scope instead of juggling endpoint calls. The follow-up clean/undo layer adds a reversible per-clip edit workflow for fillers, silence buffers, trim edges, and optional mistake cuts.
validated_outcome: go test ./..., go build ./..., go vet ./..., verify-skill, and dry-run smoke tests for insert-file, add-broll, replace-word-ranges, apply-storyboard, and format pass.

reason: Stale transcript routes, incomplete syncs, cached export status, and outdated thumbnail parameters can return missing words, unfinished downloads, or the wrong frame; preserve fetch errors, uncached polling, progress and download URLs, --inpoint-ms compatibility, and the hidden deprecated --inbox-limit flag. Derive batch operations from the live spec rather than the archived snapshot, keep deterministic supported-type errors and the 1–200 operation limit, and validate required zoom scale from flags and stdin in the API range 1–3.5. Verify credential acceptance through an uncached account request and retain milestone counts of 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100 and 500 views so automation never mistakes key presence for working auth or view counts for percentages. List responses are envelopes with a cursor param: archive and sync must unwrap them, store empty lists as zero records, and --filter-types accepts comma lists as documented while retaining JSON arrays.
validated_outcome: TestTranscriptReadAliasesUseLiveRoute, TestGetTranscriptQueryAndValidation, TestTranscriptReadCaptionsAndDiff, TestTranscriptsSyncFailsOnTranscriptFetch, TestTranscriptReadTermRangesUseLiveRoute, TestTranscriptReadUncutParsers, TestCutWordsDryRunUsesLiveTranscriptQuery, TestTranscriptReadNovelWorkflows, TestStoryboardReportsTranscriptReadError, and TestCodeOrchTranscriptReadsUseLiveRoute cover routing, query validation, live word shapes, and visible failures. TestExportsWaitHTTP/Completed asserts queued-to-running-to-completed polling, the exact %2F request URI, progress and URL; Failed, Timeout, PostFailed, PostError and GetError assert nonzero exits with JSON results; TopLevelCompleted and TestExportsWaitDryRun preserve compatibility. TestThumbnailInpointSendsStartTimeMs (video, clip, source) asserts GET paths, startTimeMs=1000, no inpointMs, response=json, empty request bodies, successful execution, and thumbnail URL output. TestVideoEditOperationsAcceptsEveryBatchType guards the exact sorted 24-type list; TestVideoEditOperationsBatchLimits guards 1–200 operations; TestVideosApplyEditsTypesHTTP checks unknown-type rejection before HTTP, preview safety, and update_text_overlay POST body and output. TestAddZoomRequiresScaleAndValidatesRange; TestDoctorVerifiesAccount; TestVideosViewedFiltersViewCounts. TestToolsManifestTranscriptReads verifies both transcript aliases use the live route and uncut metadata requires includeCut=true. TestWorkflowArchiveEnvelopePagination covers cursor paging, per-ID rows without singleton envelopes, empty resources, stderr progress, JSON output, full and incremental runs, and resumable fetch failures; TestSyncEmptyEnvelope covers empty wrapper arrays and preserved single objects; TestWebhooksCreateEndpointFilterTypes checks comma lists and JSON arrays in POST filterTypes. These three HTTP tests compile but execution is unverified here because the sandbox denies httptest socket binding.

reason: Two related issues: (1) cmd.Help() returns nil so missing positional args silently exited rc=0 in 51 generated commands; (2) parent commands without Run/RunE are non-Runnable in cobra v1.9.1, so `videos garbage` returned flag.ErrHelp (rc=0) before Args validation could run. Fix: make parents Runnable with a RunE that errors on unknown subcommand.
validated_outcome: playlists update --name x (missing <id>) exits rc=2; videos garbage exits rc=3 with 'unknown command'; bare parent (videos with no subcommand) still exits rc=0 with help; valid subcommands still dispatch.

reason: Empty results from videos viewed against a workspace with real views (622 total) was confusing. The rollup is keyed off video.viewed/video.milestone webhook events, not the API counter — empty results don't mean zero views, they mean no view events have hit the inbox yet.
validated_outcome: videos viewed --help now explains the data source and points users to wire a webhook endpoint.
